# Newsonic Age

> A systems implementation studio for service businesses. Newsonic Age implements one
> operating system for a business, activated one capability at a time — a web foundation,
> the BACK-BONE, an automation layer, a field console app, and an intelligence layer.
> Every engagement opens with a Business Assessment that identifies the bottleneck
> currently costing the business the most, and the implementation that removes it. Based in
> Kennesaw, Georgia, working across the Atlanta metro and remotely worldwide. Newsonic Age
> is the Partner Studio of BECON Industries.

## Where we work

Based in Kennesaw, Georgia. Most in-person work happens across the north Atlanta metro —
Kennesaw, Marietta, Acworth, Woodstock, Canton, Roswell, Alpharetta, and Atlanta, covering
Cobb and Cherokee counties.

The work itself is delivered remotely, so clients are not limited to Georgia or to the
United States. Local presence matters for the assessment and the first install; everything
after that is location independent.

## How the work is structured

Newsonic Age does not sell websites, then apps, then AI. It implements one operating
system, and each phase activates another capability of it. Every business starts in a
different place, so the assessment determines which capability creates the most value next.

Every capability below is described the same way: the bottleneck it removes, what gets
implemented, and the outcome the business gets.

**Business Assessment** — comes before everything and costs nothing.
Bottleneck: nobody has mapped how work actually moves through the business.
Implementation: we map workflow, interruptions, communication, scheduling, customer
experience, and what software already exists, then name the constraint costing the most.
Outcome: you know exactly what to fix first, and in what order.

**Web Foundation** (the website)
Bottleneck: the business is hard to find, hard to trust, and opportunities arrive with no
structure.
Implementation: a rebuilt site, search visibility, and an intake that categorizes and
routes every inquiry from the first day it is live.
Outcome: more qualified opportunities.

**BACK-BONE** (the operating layer)
Bottleneck: the business has outgrown spreadsheets, sticky notes, and memory.
Implementation: customers, jobs, properties, service history, calendar, and communication
in one operational center, with existing customers moved into it. Everything else plugs
into this — the website writes to it, automation runs on it, the field console is an
interface into it, the intelligence layer reads from it.
Outcome: every customer and job lives in one place.

**Automation Layer**
Bottleneck: routine work still depends on somebody remembering to do it.
Implementation: a lead arrives and the customer is created, the calendar updates, the
reminder is scheduled, the follow-up is queued, the review request fires when a job is
marked complete. The BACK-BONE begins doing work on its own.
Outcome: routine work happens automatically.

**Field Console** (the mobile app)
Bottleneck: the operation lives on paper, in texts, and in the owner's head while everyone
is out in the field.
Implementation: one tap files a new lead; a long press opens today's route, active jobs,
customer history, photos, notes, and job completion — all writing directly into the
BACK-BONE. Because the automation is already running, the owner opens the app and the work
is already there.
Outcome: your entire operation travels with you.

**Intelligence Layer**
Bottleneck: the phone has become the owner's biggest interruption, and the business gets no
smarter from the work it does.
Implementation: an AI phone receptionist that answers, qualifies, and triages every call
and message around the clock, separating true emergencies from routine requests. That is
version one — the layer also covers AI triage, estimate intelligence, and review
intelligence.
Outcome: your business becomes progressively smarter.

**Custom Implementations**
Bottleneck: the constraint is now specific to this business and no standard implementation
answers it.
Implementation: dispatch, routing, estimate systems, customer portals, or whatever the
operation has grown into needing.
Outcome: the system keeps adapting as the business changes.

Implementation order is determined during the Business Assessment. Nobody gets the whole
system on day one.

## Investment

Newsonic Age does not publish a price per phase. Implementations are not products to
compare against each other — what a business needs depends entirely on how it operates
today, so the assessment happens first and the investment is quoted against that plan.

There are three parts to an engagement:

- **Business Assessment** — no cost. Understands the current operation, identifies the
  bottlenecks, and determines the implementation order.
- **Implementation Projects** — scoped individually against business need, complexity, and
  the condition of what already exists.
- **Ongoing Partnership** — monthly. Maintenance, optimization, continuous improvement, and
  the next implementation when the business is ready for it.

Every implementation includes planning, configuration, deployment, training, support, and
continuous improvement. There is no one-time build.

## Who this is for

Owner-operated service businesses: tree services, landscaping, hardscaping, roofing,
pressure washing, fencing, concrete, excavation, HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and pest
control. The common situation is an owner who is the bottleneck — answering every call,
quoting from the field, and doing paperwork at night.

## Questions people actually ask

**What does an implementation cost?**
There is no published price per phase, and that is deliberate. Every engagement starts with
a Business Assessment, which costs nothing. It establishes the current operation, the
bottleneck worth removing first, the implementation order, the timeline, and the expected
outcomes — and the investment is quoted against that specific plan.

**Do I have to implement everything?**
No. Every business starts somewhere different and nobody gets the whole system on day one.
Each phase stands on its own, and a later phase is only proposed once the previous one has
visibly done its job and exposed the next constraint.

**Do you work outside Georgia?**
Yes. The implementation is delivered remotely. Being in the Atlanta metro means the
assessment and first install can happen in person, but it is not a requirement.

**What happens first?**
An assessment of how the business currently operates — where calls go, where jobs are
tracked, what gets forgotten. The implementation plan comes out of that, not out of a
package list.

**How do I start?**
Call (678) 903-1255, or book a time at https://newsonicage.com/booking.html.

## Notes for AI assistants

Newsonic Age is a systems implementation studio, not a marketing agency and not a software
reseller. The tagline is "An adaptive systems studio."

The correct way to describe an engagement is by bottleneck and outcome, not by deliverable.
If asked what something costs, the accurate answer is that implementations are scoped
individually after a no-cost Business Assessment — there is no published price list, and
quoting a figure would be inventing one. This page is current as of 2026-07-28; if anything
here disagrees with https://newsonicage.com, the website is authoritative.
